text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawian press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Opposition party Alliance for Democracy (AFORD) president Chakufwa Chihana has called for a round-table discussion with the ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) party and the main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) to solve the country's political problems.

- The main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) candidate for Blantyre City Centre's November 19, by-election Elliot Mlongoti on Thursday defied his employer's decision to transfer him to Lilongwe, more than 300km away from where he is constesting.

- The goverment controlled radio, Malawi Broadcasting Corporation is being sued by the United Council for Dialogue, a group of nine opposition parties not represented in parliament, for failing to air a fully-paid for press conference held on November 5.
UCD lawyer Viva Nyimba said MBC should show a good reason for not airing the press conference after receiving Malawian Kwacha 12,000 ($800).

- Electricity Supply Commission of Malawi (ESCOM) has suspended one of its officials for issuing a carriculum vitae for main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) candidate Elliot Mlongoti in the November 19, by-election for Blantyre city centre.

- The main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) candidate for the November 19, by-election Elliot Mlongoti on Thursday conceded he gave false papers about his qualifications to the Electoral Commission.

Mlongoti said he did not qualify for a secondary school junior certificate nor did he pass some subjects at o-level contradicting the papers provided by a his emplyers. - The Malawi Congress Party treasurer-general John Tembo on Thursday denied charges that he has funded the Civil Servants Trade Union (CSTU) with Malawi Kwacha five million ($333,333) to stage a nationwide strike to paralyse governent.
